title: Traffic Garden: heterogenous SSE/WS streaming chat load harness with p95/regression gates
creator: Priya Shah
description: Build a scalable, production-like load harness (Traffic Garden) for streaming chat/completions using both Server-Sent Events (SSE) and WebSocket protocols. This harness must simulate a heterogeneous client mix (short/long sessions, cold/warm KV cache, varying sequence-length distributions), measure tokens/sec and per-request latency distributions (p50/p95/p99), and provide automated regression detection against a golden baseline. The output should feed dashboards and the regression alerting pipeline so that model/runtime changes trigger actionable signals. The harness must be reproducible, parameterizable, and support deterministic seed modes for CI smoke runs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Harness can run 10k concurrent simulated session mix across SSE and WS protocols with configurable tenancy and KV-cache warmup profiles.
- Per-run metrics include overall tokens/sec, per-client tokens/sec distribution, p50/p95/p99 latency for first-token and tail tokens, end-to-end throughput, error rates, and KV cache hit/miss ratios.
- Regression detector computes rolling-window comparisons to a golden baseline using bootstrapped confidence intervals and flags >5% p95 regression with >95% confidence.
- Outputs integrate with the Console metrics ingestion pipeline and provide run artifacts (raw token traces, session timelines, and sample transcripts) uploaded to S3.
- CI mode completes in <= 20 minutes for a small synthetic mix and exits nonzero on detected regressions.
- Documentation and runbook live in Confluence with playbook for investigating alerts.
plan: 1) Define client mix profiles and sequence-length distributions (short chat, longform completion, interactive turn-based). 2) Implement protocol adapters: SSE driver and WebSocket driver that share a common workload generator API. 3) Add KV-cache warmup layers and token-watermark pacing to emulate realistic token emission patterns. 4) Instrument per-token timing, per-session traces, and aggregate counters. 5) Implement regression detection library (rolling-window, bootstrap CI, EWMA baselines) and integrate with alerting hooks. 6) Wire outputs to Console ingestion and S3 artifact uploads. 7) Run calibration experiments and tune synthetic mix to mirror production traffic metrics. 8) Add CI smoke harness + deterministic seeds.
notes: Design decision: use a shared Go runtime for drivers to minimize serialization overhead and allow precise per-token timing. Python shim will be offered for quick experiments but not used for large-scale runs.
Trade-off: bootstrap CI gives robust regression detection at cost of compute; we will run full bootstrap only in nightly/regression pipelines and use cheaper EWMA gating in presubmit.
Performance goal: sustained tokens/sec per GPU observed in production-like model variants should be matchable within +/-15% by Traffic Garden when run with the same KV cache warmup policy.
Data retention: raw token traces are sensitive; persist only sampled traces and redact prompt content per privacy guidelines. Full traces are stored encrypted in a restricted S3 prefix.
updates: 2026-02-21: Kickoff meeting with Serving Runtime and Observability teams. Agreed on metrics schema and SLI tags (session_id, tenant_id, model, protocol, seq_len_bucket).
2026-02-26: Prototype SSE driver implemented; validated single-client token pacing against real hosted endpoint. Initial p95 for first-token matched production within 12%.
2026-03-03: WebSocket adapter merged (PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pulls/1987). Added session churn mechanics (connect/disconnect jitter).
2026-03-05: Regression detector prototype using bootstrap CI completed. Baseline run captured. Deterministic seeding supported. Running nightly calibration to determine baseline variance.

2026-03-10: Integrated artifact upload to S3 (s3://redwood-traffic-garden/archives/) and wired top-line tokens/sec metric into Console ingestion (dashboard id: dg-traffic-garden-01). Observability team requested additional shard attribution tags.
risks: Large-scale bootstrap CI runs are costly; we need budget approval for nightly full bootstrap.
Emulating exact KV cache behavior for private deployments may be difficult without access to customer workload traces; calibration may diverge.
Protocol-level differences (e.g., framing differences between client SDKs) could cause small but systematic latency deviations; we will add protocol fuzzing to the harness.
next_steps: Finish shard attribution tags (ENG-582920) and add to Console payloads.
Add presubmit EWMA gating to the regression pipeline to reduce noisy developer interruptions.
Schedule calibration run against dedicated capacity cluster and capture baseline variance for 7 days.
Prepare runbook and oncall playbook for Traffic Garden alerts.
